vocabulary.pt: mexendo no jardim, com as plantas

warmUps.tr: O que ela andou fazendo? · She’s = she is ou she has.

why.0: She’s gardening é agora, neste segundo. Ela parou, mas as mãos mostram o que ela fez até agora: She’s been gardening.
why.2: Falta o been: She has been gardening, ou She’s been gardening.

warmUps.now: Your teacher says a number and asks. Answer: He’s been … · She’s been …

why.0: He’s going to swim = ele vai nadar (ainda não foi). O cabelo molhado mostra que ele já nadou: He’s been swimming.
why.1: Ele não está nadando agora. O cabelo mostra o que ele fez: He’s been swimming.

warmUps.now: Now you choose a number. Ask your teacher: What has he been doing?

warmUps.ctx: Leo works a lot. Now he’s free.
warmUps.tr: O que você tem feito ultimamente? · lately = ultimamente · a lot = muito · free = livre
o: I worked a lot last year.

why.1: I’m working now = estou trabalhando agora, neste segundo. A Kim ia achar que ele está ocupado e não pode falar. Ele está livre; o que ele vem fazendo ultimamente é I’ve been working a lot.
why.2: Last year = o ano passado, que já acabou. A Kim perguntou de ultimamente: I’ve been working a lot.

warmUps.now: Ask Leo one follow-up question about his work. Start with What or How long.

pronunciation.tip: O been é curto, “bin”, e cola no she’s: “xizbin-râning”. Não diga “bín” nem “bein”.

c: “eu venho pintando (o foco é a atividade; pode ou não estar pronto)”
pronunciation.tip: Ouça o fim: “pêinted” termina em “-ted”; “pêinting” termina em “-in”, com o “bin” antes.

dialogue.g: Oi, Ana! Voltei! Nossa… a sua sala está azul!
dialogue.text: Hi, Ana! I’m back! Wow… your living room is blue!

dialogue.g: Bem-vinda de volta! É, passei a semana toda pintando.
dialogue.text: Welcome back! Yeah, I’ve been painting all week.

dialogue.g: Quase. Pintei os dois cômodos, a sala e a cozinha. O quarto é o próximo.
dialogue.text: Almost. I’ve painted both rooms, the living room and the kitchen. The bedroom is next.

dialogue.g: E esse tênis! Você anda correndo?
dialogue.text: And your shoes! Have you been running?

dialogue.g: Sim! Estou correndo toda manhã há duas semanas.
dialogue.text: Yes! I’ve been running every morning for two weeks.

dialogue.g: Toda manhã? Nossa. E tem um bolo na mesa. Você até anda fazendo bolo!
dialogue.text: Every morning? Wow. And there’s a cake on the table. You’ve even been baking!

dialogue.g: Ha! Sim. Fiz três bolos esta semana. Enfim, como foi a Coreia?
dialogue.text: Ha! Yes. I’ve baked three cakes this week. Anyway, how was Korea?

dialogue.g: Ótima! Visitei a minha família e comi muito. Mas estou com jet lag. Passei o dia todo dormindo!
dialogue.text: Great! I visited my family and ate a lot. But I have jet lag. I’ve been sleeping all day!

dialogue.g: Ah, não! Você parece cansada. Toma, come um pedaço de bolo.
dialogue.text: Oh no! You seem tired. Here, have some cake.

dialogue.g: Claro! Eu sempre digo sim para bolo.
dialogue.text: Of course! I always say yes to cake.

comprehension.q: What has Ana been doing all week?
How long has Ana been running?
What has Kim been doing all day? Why?
comprehension.a: She’s been sleeping. She has jet lag.

grammar: How long have you been running? — For two weeks.
a Kim passou o dia dormindo (Kim’s = Kim has)
I’ve baked three cakes this week.

corrections.a: I’ve been running for two weeks.
corrections.why: “Estou correndo há duas semanas” vira have been + -ing, com for.

corrections.s: She’s been touching the guitar all day.
corrections.a: She’s been playing the guitar all day.
corrections.why: Tocar um instrumento é play: playing the guitar. Touch é encostar, pôr a mão; quem ouve imagina outra coisa.

corrections.s: How long are you studying English?
corrections.a: How long have you been studying English?
corrections.why: Para “há quanto tempo”: How long have you been studying English? Use have + been + -ing.

corrections.s: I’ve been baking three cakes this week.
corrections.a: I’ve baked three cakes this week.
corrections.why: Para contar três bolos terminados: I’ve baked three cakes. O contínuo pode descrever o trabalho, mas não afirma que os três ficaram prontos.
corrections.pre: Three cakes are finished. Report the result.

corrections.s: Leo and Carla have both been visiting places for three weeks.
corrections.why: A atividade até agora, com o tempo: have been + -ing.

steps: Reveal a clue. Ask Kim what she has been doing and for how long.
Choose an activity. Let Kim ask questions and guess it.
Choose one of Kim’s activities. Compare it with yours, ask a follow-up and mention a result.
homework: Say what you’ve been doing this week, how long and one thing you’ve finished.
Ask three follow-up questions with What, How long and Have you…?
Bring two examples from your life: I’ve been… and I’ve finished…

listening.transcript: Hi, Ana! It’s Leo. Carla and I are getting married! Next year! Sorry I haven’t called. We’ve been visiting places for the party for three weeks. We’ve seen eleven places. Eleven! I mean… every weekend, another place. Carla loves big parties. Me? I love barbecues in the park! Call me!

questions.q: Leo and Carla are getting married.
They’ve been visiting places for three days.
(How does Leo feel?) Leo loves visiting all these places.
questions.say: No. He’s tired. Carla loves big parties, but he loves barbecues.
